main_text.p: Thaleros : Quæritur quot ex his quisq; accipiat? Colloco sic:
Et dico tria continentur in 5 semel : noto 1 in semicirculo, inquiens : semel 3 sunt 3, quæ subtraho à 5 & remanent 2, quæ supra scribo.
Deinde transfero Divisorem sub 4, dicens: 3 in 24 continentur 8, & 8 in semicirculo noto, inquiens, ter 8 sunt 24, quæ sub-scripta subtraho, remanet nihil.
Tertiò transfero Divisorem sub 3, dicens: 3 in 3 continentur 1: scribo 1 in semicirculo, inquiens: semel 3 sunt 3, quæ subtraho & remanet nihil.
Quartò transfero Divisorem sub 1, & dico: 3 in 1 non continentur: scribo igitur o in semicirculo, inquiens, ter o est o, quam subtraho ab 1 & remanet 1.
Quintò transfero Divisorem, & dico 3 in 12 continentur 4, 4 in semicirculo noto, dicens: ter 4 sunt 12, quæ subtraho remanet nihil, hoc modo:

page.notes: The handwritten formula in ink above "Et dico" (the line beginning "7(5 4 3 ..." with "(1810" at its right) is manuscript annotation, not printed text, so it is left out. The printed symbol block at the foot uses arithmetic signs that I could not read reliably; the symbols are marked [?] and the numbers are copied as they appear. The long s in "Divisorem" and "scripta" has been written as plain s. The line "Thaleros" begins mid-sentence and is marked cont="true".
